title: Simultaneous Unimodularity of Positive Integer Matrices and Their Entrywise Cubes
summary: We solve an open problem posed by Richard Guy in his book Unsolved Problems in Number Theory. We prove that, for every integer $n\geq10$, there exist infinitely many $n\times n$ integer matrices $A$ such that every entry is $\ge2$ and $\det A=\det A^{[3]}=1$, where $A^{[3]}$ denotes the entrywise cube of $A$. The matrices may be chosen compatibly, so they can form the leading principal blocks of a single infinite positive integer array.
